```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("../R/helpers.R")
suppressMessages({library(knitr); library(presize); library(MKmisc); library(pROC); library(MASS); library(VCA)})
select <- dplyr::select
```

Tags: **[S]** primary public source, **[Y]** my synthesis, **[A]** assumption. Every number below is computed two ways (package vs hand, or hand vs simulation).

## (a) Concept

| Goal | Quantity to fix | Typical output |
|---|---|---|
| Estimate Se or Sp precisely | CI half-width *d*, expected Se/Sp, prevalence | n cases, then total n = cases / prevalence |
| Show Se (or Sp) exceeds a **performance goal** | goal p0, expected p1, α, power | n cases (exact binomial) |
| Show AUC > AUC0 or estimate AUC precisely | expected AUC, null, group ratio | n cases and controls |
| PPA/NPA vs a comparator | as Se/Sp but denominators are *comparator*-positive/negative | total n via comparator prevalence |
| Precision studies | days, runs, replicates | degrees of freedom → CI width |
| LoB/LoD | number of blanks and low samples | precision of the percentile / SD |

Total n is driven by the **rarest class**: for sensitivity you need cases, and cases arrive at the rate of the prevalence. [Y]

## (b) Anchor

| Item | Verified fact | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Buderer 1996 | "Statistical methodology: I. Incorporating the prevalence of disease into the sample size calculation for sensitivity and specificity." Acad Emerg Med 3(9):895-900. Sample size from desired precision, hypothesised Se/Sp and prevalence | [S] abstract |
| Flahault et al. 2005 | J Clin Epidemiol 58(8):859-862. Case numbers for expected sensitivity 0.60-0.99 and acceptable lower 95% limit 0.50-0.98, with 5% probability the estimated lower limit falls below the acceptable level | [S] abstract; tables not opened |
| Hanley & McNeil 1982 | Radiology 143(1):29-36. SE formulas for AUC; AUC = P(case > control) | [S] abstract |
| Obuchowski | AJR 2000;175:603-8 "Sample size tables for ROC studies" (multi-observer imaging). The 1994 Invest Radiol paper is also a candidate; **the citation in the brief is ambiguous** | [S] metadata |
| IVDR Annex XIII Part A 2.3.2 | The clinical performance study plan must justify statistical design and population size (items (j), (m)) | [S] |
| Design counts in EP05/EP17 (days, blanks) | Public: EP05-A3 20×2×2. EP17 counts *not verified: paywalled* | – |

## (c) R lab

### 1. Estimate Se/Sp to a target half-width

Expected Se = 0.90, half-width ±0.05, prevalence 0.20.

```{r halfwidth}
d <- 0.05; se <- 0.90; prev <- 0.20
hand_wald <- n_buderer(se, d, prev)                               # Buderer, normal approximation
pz <- prec_sens(se, prev = prev, conf.width = 2 * d)              # Wilson-based (presize)
cases_wald <- ceiling(qnorm(.975)^2 * se * (1 - se) / d^2)
kable(data.frame(Method = c("Buderer / Wald (hand)", "presize Wilson"),
                 `Cases` = c(cases_wald, ceiling(pz$n)),
                 `Total n at prevalence 0.20` = c(hand_wald, ceiling(pz$ntot)),
                 check.names = FALSE))
# simulation: achieved Wilson half-width at n = 141 cases
set.seed(71)
hw <- replicate(5000, { x <- rbinom(1, 141, se); w <- ci_wilson(x, 141); (w[["upper"]] - w[["lower"]]) / 2 })
c(sim_mean_halfwidth = mean(hw))
```

Wald slightly under-sizes relative to Wilson at p = 0.9 (139 vs 141 cases); the simulation confirms the Wilson design reaches ±0.05. [Y]

### 2. Prevalence inflates the total n

```{r prev-infl}
pv <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40)
kable(data.frame(Prevalence = pv,
  `Total n for Se +-0.05` = sapply(pv, function(p) ceiling(prec_sens(0.9, prev = p, conf.width = 0.1)$ntot)),
  `Total n for Sp +-0.05` = sapply(pv, function(p) ceiling(prec_spec(0.9, prev = p, conf.width = 0.1)$ntot)),
  check.names = FALSE), caption = "Se = Sp = 0.90. Rare condition: huge n for sensitivity")
```

When prevalence is low, enrich (case-control or stratified sampling) and state the consequence: PPV/NPV cannot be read from an enriched sample without reweighting. [Y]

### 3. Show sensitivity beats a performance goal (exact test)

Expected Se p1 = 0.90, goal p0 = 0.80, one-sided α = 0.025 (matches a two-sided 95% CI), power 80%.

```{r goal}
n_hand <- n_exact_goal_stable(0.90, 0.80, alpha = 0.025, power = 0.80)
n_mk   <- power.diagnostic.test(sens = 0.9, delta = 0.1, power = 0.8, sig.level = 0.025, prev = 0.2)$n
# simulation: power at n_hand with exact one-sided binom.test
set.seed(72)
pw <- mean(replicate(4000, binom.test(rbinom(1, n_hand, .9), n_hand, p = .8, alternative = "greater")$p.value < .025))
# closed-form normal approximation
za <- qnorm(.975); zb <- qnorm(.80)
n_norm <- ceiling(((za * sqrt(.8 * .2) + zb * sqrt(.9 * .1)) / (.9 - .8))^2)
kable(data.frame(Method = c("exact, hand (stable)", "MKmisc::power.diagnostic.test", "normal approximation", "simulated power at n(hand)"),
                 Value = c(n_hand, n_mk, n_norm, round(pw, 3))))
stopifnot(n_hand == n_mk)
```

Exact power is a **sawtooth** in n (discreteness); report the smallest n above which power never falls below target. Total n = cases / prevalence. [Y] My reading of Flahault 2005 is the same type of calculation (expected Se vs an acceptable lower limit); its tables were not opened.

```{r sawtooth}
#| fig-height: 3.2
ns <- 40:200
plot(ns, sapply(ns, power_exact_goal, p1 = .9, p0 = .8), type = "l", xlab = "cases", ylab = "exact power")
abline(h = .8, lty = 2); abline(v = n_hand, lty = 3)
```

### 4. AUC

Expected AUC 0.90; test against AUC0 = 0.75, two-sided α = 0.05, 80% power, 1:1 cases:controls.

```{r auc}
n_h <- n_auc_hm(0.90, 0.75, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80)
# simulation with the binormal model: AUC = pnorm(delta/sqrt(2)) for equal unit variances
delta <- function(a) sqrt(2) * qnorm(a)
set.seed(73)
sim_power <- function(n, a1 = 0.90, a0 = 0.75, reps = 600) {
  mean(replicate(reps, {
    cs <- rnorm(n, delta(a1)); ct <- rnorm(n)
    r <- roc(rep(1:0, each = n), c(cs, ct), quiet = TRUE, direction = "<")
    ci <- ci.auc(r, method = "delong")            # reject if the lower 95% limit exceeds AUC0
    (as.numeric(ci)[1] > a0)
  }))
}
grid <- c(20, 24, 28, n_h)
kable(data.frame(`Cases = controls` = grid, `Simulated power` = sapply(grid, sim_power),
                 check.names = FALSE),
      caption = sprintf("Hanley-McNeil n = %d per group; power by simulation (600 reps)", n_h))
```

The Hanley–McNeil formula is **conservative** here: the simulated power at its n is well above 80%, and 80% is reached with fewer subjects. The simulated rule (DeLong lower 95% limit > AUC0) is a one-sided α = 0.025 test, which is the same critical value as the two-sided 0.05 used in the formula, so the gap comes from the variance approximation, not the α. Use the formula to plan, simulation to confirm. [Y]

Cross-check against `pROC::power.roc.test` (which handles AUC vs 0.5 only) and `presize` (CI half-width):

```{r auc2}
n_h5 <- n_auc_hm(0.75, 0.5, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80)
pr <- power.roc.test(auc = 0.75, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80)
kable(data.frame(Check = c("HM hand, AUC 0.75 vs 0.5", "pROC::power.roc.test, same"),
                 `Cases (= controls)` = c(n_h5, ceiling(pr$ncases)), check.names = FALSE))
# precision: n for 95% CI width 0.10 at AUC 0.90, prevalence 0.4
pa <- prec_auc(0.9, prev = 0.4, conf.width = 0.10)
hm_hw <- function(n1) 1.96 * sqrt(var_auc_hm(0.9, n1, 1.5 * n1))
n1_hand <- ceiling(uniroot(function(n1) hm_hw(n1) - 0.05, c(10, 2000))$root)
c(presize_cases = ceiling(pa$n1), HM_hand_cases = n1_hand)
```

### 5. PPA/NPA and the indeterminate fraction

When intermediates count as non-agreement, the quantity to size is PPA_incl = Se_det·(1 − f_D) where f_D is the intermediate fraction among comparator-positives.

```{r indet}
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30), function(f) {
  p1 <- 0.94 * (1 - f)                         # assumed determinate sensitivity 0.94
  data.frame(`Intermediate fraction` = f, `Expected PPA incl.` = round(p1, 3),
    `Cases for +-0.05 (Wilson)` = ceiling(prec_sens(p1, conf.width = 0.10, prev = 1)$n),
    `Total n needed for 300 determinate cases` = ceiling(300 / (1 - f)), check.names = FALSE)}))
kable(tab, caption = "Se among determinate = 0.94 [A]")
```

Two decisions to pre-specify: the endpoint **including** vs excluding indeterminates, and the sample size to secure enough *determinate* results (divide by 1 − f). [Y]

### 6. Design sizes for EP05 and EP17-type studies (illustrative)

**Precision, CI width of within-lab SD versus number of days.** Satterthwaite df of the sum of mean squares; hand check against VCA's DF for the Day 2 data.

```{r ep05}
sat_df <- function(ms, D, R, K) {
  cf <- c(day = 1 / (R * K), run = (R - 1) / (R * K), err = (K - 1) / K)
  df <- c(D - 1, D * (R - 1), D * R * (K - 1))
  sum(cf * ms)^2 / sum((cf * ms)^2 / df)
}
# MS from the Day 2 simulated study (VCA output): day 9.906929, run 5.628042, error 4.808839
df_hand <- sat_df(c(9.906929, 5.628042, 4.808839), 20, 2, 2)
c(hand = df_hand, VCA_reported = 69.815065)
stopifnot(abs(df_hand - 69.815065) < 1e-3)

ci_ratio <- function(D, R = 2, K = 2, sd_d = 1.2, sd_r = 1.5, sd_e = 2) {
  ms <- c(sd_e^2 + K * sd_r^2 + R * K * sd_d^2, sd_e^2 + K * sd_r^2, sd_e^2)
  df <- sat_df(ms, D, R, K)
  c(days = D, df = df, `upper/estimate` = sqrt(df / qchisq(.025, df)), `lower/estimate` = sqrt(df / qchisq(.975, df)))
}
kable(t(sapply(c(5, 10, 20, 30, 40), ci_ratio)), digits = 3,
      caption = "Expected 95% CI of within-lab SD as multiples of the estimate (2 runs x 2 replicates)")
```

**LoB: precision of the 95th percentile vs number of blanks.**

```{r lob-n}
set.seed(74)
sim_lob <- function(n, B = 4000) {
  p <- replicate(B, { b <- rnorm(n); c(np = unname(quantile(b, .95, type = 6)), par = mean(b) + 1.645 * sd(b)) })
  data.frame(blanks = n, `SD nonparametric` = sd(p["np", ]), `SD parametric` = sd(p["par", ]),
             `theory SD parametric` = sqrt(1 / n + 1.645^2 / (2 * (n - 1))), check.names = FALSE)
}
kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(c(20, 60, 120, 240), sim_lob)), digits = 3,
      caption = "Blank ~ N(0,1): SD of the LoB estimate (units of the blank SD)")
```

The parametric estimator is more precise (it uses all data and the normal assumption); the closed form `sqrt(1/n + 1.645²/(2(n−1)))` agrees with the simulation. [Y]
